cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 answers T1's verdict; T6 concedes T5; T9 calls T8's resentment point the hinge.
cells.limitation: T8 pivots to a new option and T11 adds a step without answering T10.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces resentment as the real question; T9 builds on it and section D splits both questions.
cells.limitation: T11's open-bid test reprises T3's going-quiet test without new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 to T6 weigh a silent test against a curious conversation; T7 raises demand versus question.
cells.limitation: Fear of learning the friend cares less stays beneath the surface across all turns.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 narrows its point after T5; T10 softens T1; section D keeps disputes open.
cells.limitation: T11 proposes another test without meeting T4's objection that silences get misread.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates what the pattern means about the friend from what it does to the user.
cells.limitation: Test-versus-conversation dispute in section D ends without saying which condition settles it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 restates T1's evidence fairly before challenging the leap from one pattern.
cells.limitation: T4 treats T3's going quiet as purely silent, skipping T3's admitted cost.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names counting first texts as the assumption; T3 answers that replying is not reaching.
cells.limitation: T11's open-bid step goes unchallenged as the final turn.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Aristotle on pleasure friendships and Gottman on bids are paraphrased accurately in T1 and T2.
cells.limitation: T5, pd=false, uses quotation marks; T1, T7, T10 bases cite book numbers.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 says it goes further than Aristotle; bases mark extensions as the speaker's own.
cells.limitation: T11 calls a week's non-response information without weighing T2's low-initiator point.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 concedes T5's point and states how it narrows the Mapper's position.
cells.limitation: T10 softens without naming T2 as cause; Realist never answers T4's objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames speaking up as a request, a test, or a risk depending on unknowns.
cells.limitation: The user's possible hurt at feeling less valued is named only indirectly in T9.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 uses the lovely meetings to make continuing to plan a real option.
cells.limitation: T5 and T11 offer generic tactics not tied to this friendship's details.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 asks whether the user would still want a replier-style friendship.
cells.limitation: T1 imposes the Realist's own test-before-investing preference on the user.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 and T9 weigh the risk of inventing a problem against unspoken resentment.
cells.limitation: How long the pattern has lasted and the friend's circumstances never enter.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on resentment, on the friend's response, and on unknown reasons.
cells.limitation: No question on pattern duration or recent life changes for the friend.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T7 distinguishes wanting them to text from genuine curiosity, framed conditionally.
cells.limitation: Motives are not laid side by side as alternatives with one answerable question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 surfaces the assumption that initiating equals interest; T4 that silence is a neutral test.
cells.limitation: Whether equal initiation is the right norm for this user is probed only in T7.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T7 sets warm meetings against reciprocity: some friendships worth keeping on those terms.
cells.limitation: The weight the user places on being sought out is left implicit.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 names a tightening each time the user opens their phone.
cells.limitation: Fear of what a direct ask might reveal is never named in any turn.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D ends with a question the user can answer about a replier-style friend.
cells.limitation: T1's acquaintance verdict is offered before the user's view is invited.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options span keep planning (T8), going quiet (T3), small ask (T5), talk (T6), open bid (T11).
cells.limitation: Section E never lists the options together before branching.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T3 names going quiet's cost; T5 the talk's risk; T8 resentment as planning's cost.
cells.limitation: T11's open-bid step is presented as costless to both people.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T9: no sting favors silence; tightening favors speaking soon, in person.
cells.limitation: T11's one-week window is not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names why the friend does not initiate as the deciding unknown.
cells.limitation: Section E does not say how to read a non-response given T2's low-initiator point.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9 suggests in person or a call; T11 a casual opening before asking.
cells.limitation: T11's step echoes the silent test T4 criticised, unaddressed.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T5 explains the risk with a plain example of a small, specific ask.
cells.limitation: Pleasure friendships in T1 go unexplained for a general reader.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'concede that' maps to T5; T9 'the hinge' to T8; T10 'first claim' to T1.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range; options unfold one per turn from T3 to T11.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths sit in a narrow band, giving a flat cadence across T1 to T11.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Realist judges reciprocity, Mapper frames talks, Bid Watcher counts small reaches.
cells.limitation: Mapper and Bid Watcher share one calm advisory register across turns.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; T3 opens with two words before advancing.
cells.limitation: T11 reprises T3's testing idea; section E repeats section D's split.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T1 raises whether this is a friendship at all; T7 whether it is worth keeping.
cells.limitation: After T7 the tension eases into advice without a sharpened stake.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 concedes T5's point and names how it narrows the Mapper's claim.
cells.limitation: T10's softening of T1 names no earlier argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: Realist's blunt 'acquaintance wearing a friend's coat' in T1.
cells.limitation: Bid Watcher and Mapper show little personal voice beyond role.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7 'a demand wearing a question'; T9 tightening when opening the phone.
cells.limitation: Vivid images come mostly from the Realist; T5 and T11 are plain.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9's hinge creates a turn from analysis to the user's own feeling.
cells.limitation: Even intensity and similar turn lengths from T1 to T11 give little rise or release.

strengths: T8 introduces resentment as the real question; T9 and section D build the debate's key split on it.
T2 and T3 exchange a genuine objection and answer: responsiveness versus reaching.
Section E gives conditions the user can observe, such as felt resentment and the friend's response.
weaknesses: T5 (Bid Watcher, pd=false) places suggested phrasings in quotation marks; bases in T1, T7, T10 cite book numbers.
The Friendship Realist never answers T4's objection to going quiet, and T10 softens without naming a cause.
Fear of what a direct ask might reveal is never named by any mind.

symptoms.observed: A pd=false turn wraps suggested wording in quotation marks.
symptoms.evidence: 'you never text first' feels like a failing they can't fix

symptoms.observed: Realist drops the going-quiet test after T4 and softens T1 without naming why.
symptoms.evidence: I'll soften my first claim. One lopsided pattern doesn't prove

symptoms.observed: No mind names fear of learning the friend values the user less.
symptoms.evidence: If you notice a tightening each time you open your phone

symptoms.observed: T11 proposes a quiet test; T4's objection that silences get misread goes unmet.
symptoms.evidence: leave it open for a week. If they pick it up

symptoms.observed: Pattern duration and friend's circumstances never asked or branched.
symptoms.evidence: Start with the evidence: you plan, they enjoy it

findings.description: Single quotation marks enclose two suggested phrasings in a pd=false turn; deterministic check also reports one such turn.
Bases cite Nicomachean Ethics book numbers (VIII-IX) from a worker that could not browse; the divisions are real but are references nonetheless.
Paraphrases of Gottman and of Stone, Patton and Heen match general knowledge of these books but no source evidence is attached.

rubric_fit_notes: The T5 quotation marks enclose suggested wording, not attributed quotations; the cap applies by the stated rule though the substance is not a misquotation.
question_type_note: Read as a relationship decision, so every cell was applied as written, with options including waiting and a limited step.
